primary.title: Crito

primary.author: Plato

secondary.title: Socrates and the Jews: The Question of Hellenism
secondary.author: Michael Prior
secondary.rationale: Examines Socrates' place within the broader intellectual landscape of the ancient world, including his relationship with Jewish thought.

suggestions.notes: Socrates himself wrote nothing. Our primary knowledge of him comes from the writings of his students, most notably Plato and Xenophon. The works listed under primary sources are attributed to Plato's dialogues, which are generally considered the most reliable accounts of Socratic thought.
